'''Only One Story''' is the Japanese opening theme for the ''[[Rayquaza Rising]]'' arc and the fourth of ''[[Pokémon Horizons: The Series]]''. It debuted in [[HZ068]], replacing {{so|Will}}. The full version of the song was first released as a [[List of Pokémon digital singles#Only One Story|digital single]] on October 11, 2024.<ref>[https://cf.zerobaseone.jp/news/detail/501 ZEROBASEONE初のアニメタイアップ！日本オリジナル新曲「Only One Story」がテレビアニメ「ポケットモンスター」オープニングテーマに決定！10月11日（金）に配信リリース！ - ZEROBASEONE Japan Official Site （ゼロベースワン オフィシャルサイト）]</ref>

A Korean version of the song, titled '''Only One Story (Korean ver.)''', is the opening theme for the Korean dub of the ''Rayqyaza Rising'' arc and the third of ''Pokémon Horizons: The Series''.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VySQWVo1KWs <nowiki>[공식] 포켓몬스터: 레쿠쟈 라이징 OP - Only One Story (Kor ver) with ZEROBASEONE - YouTube</nowiki>]</ref> It debuted in [[HZ068]], replacing {{so|Will|Will -Korean ver.-}}. The full version of the song was released as a digital single on April 15, 2025.<ref>[https://x.com/ZB1_official/status/1912071713485131936 ZEROBASEONE on Twitter/X]</ref>

==Opening animation==
===Synopsis===
Clouds are blowing fast in the sky when the [[Black Rayquaza]] appears and flies over them. [[Liko]], [[Roy]], [[Dot]], {{TP|Liko|Floragato}}, {{TP|Roy|Crocalor}}, {{TP|Dot|Quaxwell}}, and [[Pagogo|Terapagos]] gaze at the sunny sky. Dot moves forward first, followed by Roy, and then Liko with Terapagos. They all run forward before stopping at the cliff, with Rayquaza flying in the distance. The series logo appears just as {{p|Rayquaza}} flies into it.

Dot's Room on the [[Brave Olivine]] is draped in purple, and Dot is at her desk as an overlay of her feeling frustrated appears. The swirling clouds in the sky are draped in red, and Roy is desperately reaching out for Rayquaza as an overlay of him feeling conflicted as he holds the Sky High Pokémon's ancient [[Poké Ball]] appears. The battlefield at [[Naranja Academy]] is draped in blue, and Liko recalls one of her fainted Pokémon back into its Poké Ball as an overlay of her feeling sad about her loss appears.

Liko's overlay becomes a transition into the next scene in a colorless background. Liko takes a step, causing green leaves to appear from under her foot. She then reaches out for the full moon with the camera zooming out from her blue eyes, which appear to be the only thing colored. Liko notices a green and sparkly shadow of {{p|Sprigatito}} running past her, followed by {{p|Fuecoco}} and {{p|Quaxly}}. They all go in front of the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]], becoming their second-stage [[Evolution]]s and turning everything colorful. Roy and Dot appear alongside Liko, and they all run towards the Rising Volt Tacklers together.

The screen turns completely white, shortly followed by a swinging transition of Liko's pendant. [[Carmine]] is in the [[Kitakami Hall]], when {{p|Sinistcha}} causes her to drop her [[Syrupy Apple]]. [[Briar]] reads the [[Scarlet Book]] at the [[Crystal Pool]], and the camera zooms in on her left earring, which turns into a transition. [[Perrin]] snaps a photo with [[Hisuian form|Hisuian]] {{p|Growlithe}} in a bamboo forest. A darker part of the forest is shown which {{p|Kleavor}}'s back turned.

[[Sidian]], [[Coral]], [[Spinel]] and [[Chalce]] appear in front of [[Gibeon]]'s monolith (which has pink mist with white orbs below it). The scene freezes for a brief moment to show the current [[Explorers]] Admins and their Pokémon; {{p|Medicham}} under Chalce's orange background of the far left, {{p|Garganacl}} under Sidian's dark red background of the center left, {{p|Glalie}} under Coral's magenta background of the center right, and {{p|Umbreon}} under Spinel's cyan background of the far right. [[Amethio]] and {{TP|Amethio|Ceruledge}} appear in front of them, heading for a whirlwind. Gibeon appears and uses the [[Laquium]]'s power.

Shiny 50% {{p|Zygarde}} appears in what appears to be [[Laqua]], facing Liko, Roy, Dot, and [[Friede]], along with {{p|Floragato}}, {{p|Crocalor}}, {{p|Quaxwell}}, and [[Captain Pikachu]]. A determined Liko tosses a Poké Ball into the air, along with four others, which all release Pokémon as Terapagos turns into its Terastal Form. Cap and Crocalor ride on {{TP|Roy|Kilowattrel}} and {{TP|Friede|Charizard}} respectively. Cap uses {{m|Thunder Punch}}, followed by Kilowattrel using {{m|Spark}}, {{TP|Liko|Hattrem}}, and {{TP|Dot|Tinkatuff}} fly past each other, both using {{m|Brutal Swing}}. Crocalor and Charizard use {{m|Flamethrower}}, followed by Quaxwell and Floragato using {{m|Liquidation}} and {{m|Magical Leaf}} respectively. The onslaught of moves ends with Zygarde meeting Rayquaza's {{m|Dragon Ascent}} head-on, creating a blast of swirling wind that tears the ground apart. After this, Terapagos appears to be in its Stellar Form, using {{m|Tera Starstorm}} to clear the sky. Rayquaza, along with [[Lucius]]'s {{p|Arboliva}}, {{rf|Galarian}} {{p|Moltres}}, and {{p|Lapras}}, flies off into the clear sky, each becoming a ray of dark-gray, green, red, and blue light that collides to create a bright yellow burst of energy.

All the Rising Volt Tacklers are outside the observation deck of the Brave Olivine overlooking the clear, sunny sky with optimism. The focus of this scene turns to Liko, Roy, and Dot, and then Captain Pikachu. Friede walks into a white screen. Amethio and Ceruledge have their backs turned on Spinel and Umbreon. Lucius is seen traveling with who looks to be a younger Gibeon and [[Rystal]], a girl dressed in green carrying Terapagos. The Brave Olivine flies over a bed of clouds next to a wide cliff. 

The opening ends with the Rising Volt Tacklers performing their handshake, the focus quickly turning to just Liko. Her Rotom Phone is next to Lucius's belt and his memoirs, the picture on it depicting an event from the previous episode.

==Variants==
#[[HZ068]] - [[HZ070]]: The original animation.
#[[HZ071]] - [[HZ073]]: The animation is updated to include [[Dot's Tinkatuff]].
#[[HZ074]] - [[HZ081]]: The clips of [[Carmine]], [[Briar]], [[Perrin]], and [[Lucius's Kleavor]] are replaced with [[Geeta]] and the [[Legendary beasts]]. Kleavor is added to the scene with the [[Six Heroes]] flying to the sky.
#[[HZ082]]: {{TP|Lucius|Gouging Fire}} is added to the scene with the Six Heroes.
#[[HZ083]] - [[HZ089]]: A silhouette of [[Laqua]] is seen behind the [[Black Rayquaza]] as it flies around the series title. Geeta and the Legendary beasts are replaced by flashback shots of [[Rystal]], [[Lucius]], [[Pagogo]], and the Black Rayquaza, followed by a scene of Pagogo falling into a hole as a desperate [[Liko]], who is wearing her pendant, reaches out to Rystal and Lucius.

==Trivia==
* This is the second consecutive [[List of Japanese opening themes|Japanese opening theme song]] of the mainline [[Pokémon animated series]] to be sung by a non-Japanese artist, as it was sung by a Korean boy band.
* This is the second consecutive [[List of Korean opening themes|Korean opening theme song]] of the mainline Pokémon animated series to have been translated directly from Japanese.
* The instrumental of this song can be heard in [[HZ116]].
* The photo shown in [[HZ089]] is the only one that doesn't depict an event from the previous episode, instead showing the Rising Volt Tacklers sometime between the events of ''[[HZ039|Tinkatink's Ideal Hammer]]'' and ''[[HZ045|From So Far Away]]''.
* Unlike the Japanese version, the Korean version uses only the first variant of the animation, and thus the photo shown on the [[Rotom Phone|Rotom Pad]] at the end does not change each episode, instead showing only the photo from [[HZ068]].
